steps.what: the even permutations of four coordinates
steps.why: the 96-block of the icosians is an EVEN-permutation orbit; taking the odd orbit instead gives a conjugate copy, which is exactly how lattice(1).html and the maths 4 ledger came to disagree in 96 of 120 elements

steps.determines: UNIQUE UP TO conjugation by a coordinate permutation
steps.expr: 8 Lipschitz (+-1,0,0,0) | 16 Hurwitz (+-1/2)^4 | 96 even perms of (0, 1/2, phi^-1/2, phi/2) with all sign patterns
steps.why: the unit group of the icosian ring; equivalently the 600-cell's vertices; equivalently 2I. The descriptions coincide and 6.3 checks that they do

steps.expr: closure of {1} under right-multiplication by s = (1+i+j+k)/2 and t = (phi + phi^-1 i + j)/2
steps.what: the same 120, generated cold from two icosians
steps.why: a SECOND, independent construction. Two constructions agreeing is evidence; two constructions nobody ever compared is a drift vector, which is what maths 4 had

steps.expr: q |-> 2q, each Z[phi] entry m + n*phi flattened to (m, n)
steps.why: icosian coordinates lie in (1/2)Z[phi]; doubling clears the halves so the lattice is integral. The factor 2 is a coordinate convention and nothing else

steps.what: a Z-basis of the icosian ring
steps.why: the icosian ring is the Z[phi]-span of the 120, so as a Z-module it is generated by each icosian together with its phi-multiple. HERMITE NORMAL FORM IS CANONICAL -- that is what turns 'computed externally by row reduction' (an answer, and basis-dependent) into a criterion whose answer is unique

steps.expr: B(x,y) = Tr(delta <x,y>), delta = phi/sqrt5; on doubled coordinates this is sum_k (m m' + m n' + n m' + 2 n n')
steps.why: restriction of scalars from Z[phi] to Z is self-dual only against the CODIFFERENT, so delta must be drawn from the inverse different (1/sqrt5) and be TOTALLY POSITIVE, or the form is not positive definite. The plain trace form fails here, and that failure is on maths 4's dead-ends list

steps.check: det G = 256, all entries even, det halfGram = 1, half diagonal even
steps.what: the Gram of the icosian ring, and its invariants
steps.why: rank 8 + even + unimodular + positive definite characterises E8 uniquely, so these four facts ARE the identification. No classification theorem is invoked and none is needed -- which is what retires the uniqueness-theorem citation

steps.check: M M^T = 2G, |det| = 256, every row in L
steps.expr: integer M with M M^T = 2G AND every row in L = {y in Z^8 : coordinates of one parity, sum = 0 mod 4}
steps.what: the isometry onto the textbook E8
steps.why: L is the doubled D8+ presentation of E8. THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS CRITERION OMITTED THE L CONDITION, and the search satisfied it with rows outside L -- a valid factorisation that is not an isometry onto the textbook lattice. An under-specified criterion is found by RUNNING it, never by reading it
